result: Line state is {basic,literal,arrayDepth}; only outside multiline strings and arrays is a line structural. Comments terminate scanning outside quotes; basic escapes skip the next character; closing brackets clamp depth at zero. Header regex is a structural recognizer, not TOML validation.

Single-line parser returns {value,start,end} at the closing quote, or null for missing close, multiline opener, CR/LF or invalid basic escape. It accepts the quoted prefix without validating trailing tokens. Basic escapes include b,t,n,f,r,quote,backslash,u4,U8; invalid hex, surrogate and out-of-range Unicode reject. Literal strings do not decode.

Multiline parser optionally drops initial LF/CRLF, normalizes CR line endings, supports basic backslash newline continuation and returns at the first closing triple quote; malformed/unterminated input returns null. It is not a full TOML grammar.

Key path parses ASCII bare or quoted segments and dots with surrounding space; returns segments/end or null. Trailing dot fails. Table path requires matching brackets and complete inner consumption; assignment callers separately require '='.

Project-header parser is a separate local parser: quoted path after projects., closing bracket and optional comment; basic decoding preserves unknown escapes rather than interpreting Unicode escapes. This differs from parseTomlSingleLineStringValue and can distinguish escaped and decoded project identities.
contracts.effects: Pure string/state transformations; no IO or rollback.

result: Sections retain original block content and start index until joining; only structural lines open a section. Exact trimmed [hooks.state] or prefix [hooks.state. is runtime hook trust; quoted/spaced aliases are not equivalent here.

Project identity delegates to the concrete project-header parser and accepted C-CODEX Windows/WSL normalization. Native Windows/ordinary UNC fold case, WSL Linux tails remain case-sensitive except drvfs, POSIX is unchanged; revocation matching folds Windows-style/WSL tails more loosely.

Duplicate project keys keep the first block unless a later block reads untrusted and the current one does not. getProjectTrustLevel is a multiline regex over the raw block, so a trust_level-looking line inside a multiline value can affect classification.

Stripping always removes recognized hook trust; removes only project keys in runtimeProjectHeaders unless their raw block reads untrusted. extractOrdinary builds a set of all projects then uses that operation, so untrusted projects survive despite its drop-every-project comment.

joinTomlBlocks trims blocks, omits empties, separates them by a blank line and appends one newline; extractOrdinary trims the final newline. Whole-output byte preservation is not promised by this implementation.
contracts.effects: Returned text feeds already-characterized promotion/mirror writes; no additional IO in these helpers.

result: Only structural single-line string assignments in recognized raw table/key locations are rewritten. Raw keys have whitespace removed; quoted key aliases, inline tables and triple-quoted values are not comprehensively interpreted.

Blank, home-prefixed, dollar/percent-shaped, POSIX/Windows absolute and URI-scheme values pass through. Classification uses trimmed value but resolution joins the original parsed value, including its spaces. sourceDir starting '/' selects posix join, otherwise win32 join.

Rewrites only the string span, preserving assignment prefix and suffix including a trailing invalid token admitted by the prefix parser. Emits literal quote when safe, otherwise escaped basic quote with control characters escaped. Unsupported/malformed values are left untouched, not converted to a structured error.
contracts.effects: Pure return string; ownership/WSL source-directory choice and write failure remain exact AL-C04 contracts.

result: Reuse the delivered integrations immediate implementations rather than classifying an unawaited launch callback as unread. Native bridge normalizes/deduplicates source homes and excludes self; regular .jsonl/.jsonl.zst walker yields in batches and skips directory errors; existing targets remain; hardlink then symlink fallback may count linked without proving provider discovery/resume.

Native in-flight coalescing is by target home, and different targets run independently. Its source/target mutations can finish after launch returns; launch return is not a completion barrier or all-history certificate.

WSL job key is the full target triple. Wrong-distro/unresolvable paths return zero summary without dispatch. Guest script has a 30-second boundary, scans only .jsonl, preserves existing targets, tries hardlink then staged copy/compare/hardlink publication and can fail after earlier files were linked.

WSL nonzero/timeout rejects internally and the background wrapper catches/logs it; malformed summary returns zeros and numeric fields are not checked for nonnegative values. No native exit or guest credential success is inferred from that parser.

contracts.effects: Partial local/guest history links remain on error; no general launch rollback or await barrier. No bridge or guest process was run here.

result: Source is shared Orca managed home/sessions; target is override || system home, plus sessions; audit/marker are in the managed backfill state directory. Existing AL home-path bodies determine directories and mkdir behavior. No remote host is inferred from a local path.

One process-global in-flight promise, not keyed by target or options, is returned to concurrent callers. Its first caller controls the pass. Caught outer failure logs and resolves null; no-work also resolves null. Identity-checked finally clears the cached promise.

FullScanRequired forces full walk; missing baseline uses requested dates if provided; otherwise union pending/requested dates, or today's UTC date for ignoreCompletionMarker, else no work. A bounded pass without baseline cannot certify one.

Returns stopped plus scannedFiles, linkedFiles, copiedFiles (always zero), skippedExistingFiles, skippedUnexpectedFiles, skippedSymlinkFiles, skippedUnsupportedFilesystemFiles, failedDirectories, failedFiles, failedHealAuditRecords. Only exact YYYY/MM/DD/rollout-*.jsonl is eligible; .jsonl.zst is not a backfill candidate.

Audit coverage is read before checking source root; missing root is empty, other root/directory failures count and append diagnostics. Date selection validates calendar round trips, deduplicates/sorts and walks only valid requested roots; a nonempty all-invalid list does not become a full scan.

Sequential publication skips source symlinks and existing target entries (including symlinks); lstat failures collapse to no stat, but link still refuses overwrite. EEXIST race records existing. EXDEV/ENOTSUP/EOPNOTSUPP/ENOSYS count unsupported and never copy; other failures increment failedFiles and permit subsequent files.

Stop is observed between files and after the pass; a single in-flight mutation can finish. Loop stop tests truthiness while final marker gate checks shouldStop() !== true. Caller callback exceptions can reject after already-written links.

Completion requires not stopped, shouldStop !== true, canWriteCompletionMarker !== false and zero failed file/directory/heal counts. Unsupported skips do not block completion. Marker-write failure can yield null after successful links; retries audit existing targets instead of rolling them back.
contracts.effects: May mkdir, hardlink, append audit, atomically write marker. No copy fallback, deletion of history, provider indexing proof or transaction rollback.

result: Ledger reader ignores blank/torn/non-object/array JSON, treats ENOENT as absent and propagates other strict read errors, closing stream in finally. File IDs hash normalized target plus stat identity/size/times; changed files receive a new healing event. Diagnostic IDs include operation/source/target/stat/error codes.

Audit append prepends newline, adds time/random record ID, creates directory and retries the identical serialized append once. Failure warns and returns false. Failed publication/existing heal records increment failedHealAuditRecords; failed diagnostic or run-summary append does not, so those failures alone can coexist with completion marker.

Marker accepts versions 3/4 with matching normalized target and full baseline (v3 implicit); zero baselineScannedFiles forces recheck, unreadable/malformed means no baseline. Numeric baseline field is type-checked but not finite/nonnegative validated. A baseline may still carry pending work.

Pending dates and live launch expand UTC range through today; more than 31 requires full scan. Dates are calendar-validated; expansion constructs the span before checking that cap. Bounded write cannot create a historical baseline. Full current-generation pass can clear pending/full demand; stale generation or retained live dates survive.

Invalidation generation is process-global, incremented before marker reading. A different-target marker is left unchanged and reports full scan owed. Pending marker write failure warns then removes the marker; if removal also fails AggregateError propagates. Normal marker writes use previously characterized atomic helper.
contracts.effects: Filesystem read/append/marker write/remove are actual local boundaries; durable flush, multi-process coordination and downstream healing consumer completion are not implied.

result: Unsupported Windows, missing home, or unsafe variable name returns undefined. Cache key is name, home, shell, configHome separated by NUL, including cached undefined; production has no invalidation call here.

Default shell is zsh; zsh reads .zshenv then exported ZDOTDIR or home/.zprofile,.zshrc,.zlogin. Bash scans all .bash_profile,.bash_login,.profile in that order, never .bashrc. Fish scans sorted conf.d/*.fish then config.fish beneath explicit trimmed XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config. Unsupported explicit shell reads nothing.

Only whole-line export NAME=value or fish set with export flag is admitted. Last nonempty matching value wins; empty assignment does not clear it. Quote-aware comment stripping does not process quote escapes. Only matching enclosing quotes are removed; HOME, ${HOME}, ~/ expand unless single-quoted. Unsets, sourced files, control flow, universal variable store and other substitutions are not executed.

Missing/unreadable startup file continues; snippet directory errors yield none. A static export on a line inside a function/conditional block is not evaluated for reachability. This is a cached hint, not proof of the eventual shell environment.

Session helper selects supplied HOME/SHELL/XDG_CONFIG_HOME with nullish process fallbacks and optional shell override. The already-read AL-C03 real-home eligibility caller remains authoritative for how undefined/custom home affects managed versus real-home routing.

result: Existing migration marker of any entry type skips state migration. Enumerates sorted immediate account directory entries with an existing home/.orca-managed-home marker; unlike auth migration, this is not canonical account-ID/regular-marker ownership validation.

History merge preserves nonempty raw lines, deduplicates exact strings, and atomically writes one final newline; it does not parse session JSON. Session walk follows root stat but ignores child symlink dirents; processes all regular files, not only rollout suffixes.

Absent session target is copied; equal bytes no-op; conflict copies to deterministic .orca-legacy-<accountID> before extension and appends best-effort diagnostic. Copy is not exclusive/CAS and an existing conflict-name file can be overwritten. Marker is written only after all homes; an error leaves earlier history/copies intact, warning and allowing retry.

Legacy active pointer migration only runs if path-exists helper succeeds; errors in that helper become absence. Already matching lexical link target is retained. Replaceable means symlink or Windows readable link; lstat errors are considered replaceable. Actual non-link directories are preserved.

Repoint creates temporary symlink/junction, renames it, and on rename failure rechecks replaceability before removing the old link and retrying rename; finally removes temporary link. That fallback can leave no pointer if the second rename fails. All safe wrapper failures warn and continue, not full rollback.

Metadata/account root uses Electron userData; shared runtime paths use existing managed home resolver (including its override behavior). No new host/distro ownership inference is introduced by importing local legacy state.
